# TrustPlane Auth

> TrustPlane Auth is an open-source, proof-bound authorization runtime for AI agents, machine clients, service APIs, and MCP/tool servers. Instead of presenting a long-lived API key or bearer token, each caller proves one specific request — bound to method, path, body, audience, and time — and a local verifier allows or denies it before it reaches the upstream API. In one line: SPIFFE authenticates workloads; the TrustPlane Passport authenticates requests.

TrustPlane Auth is built for security, platform, and infrastructure teams shipping agentic and machine-to-machine workflows that should not depend on broad, long-lived machine credentials. It is open source and runs locally and offline — no hosted account, database, or mandatory phone-home.

## Category
- Open-source machine authorization, AI agent authorization, MCP / tool-server authorization, service-to-service (machine-to-machine) authorization, non-human identity authorization, API-key alternative, proof-bound (request-bound) authorization.

## What TrustPlane Auth is
- A proof-bound authorization runtime that verifies a short-lived TrustPlane Passport plus a per-request transcript-v1 proof before a request reaches a protected API.
- A local-first verifier you run yourself: a brownfield reverse-proxy adapter, Go library middleware, or a broker + sidecar — enforcement happens in your own infrastructure with no required hosted service.
- A signed trust-and-policy bundle model for route/source authorization, with atomic replay protection so each proof is one-time.
- Complementary to the identity you already have: SPIFFE/SPIRE, OIDC/JWT, or a local issuer.

## What TrustPlane Auth is not
- Not API-key management: it does not rotate or hide a reusable shared secret; it verifies fresh proof for each request.
- Not bearer-only OAuth ingress, and not generic IAM: the protected application still owns tenant, role, entitlement, and resource decisions.
- Not a SPIFFE replacement or SPIFFE-only wrapper, not a service mesh, not a CA replacement, not a secrets manager, not a payment network or marketplace.

## How it works
1. A caller already has a workload identity (SPIFFE/SPIRE, an OIDC/JWT issuer, or a local TrustPlane issuer).
2. It obtains a short-lived, audience-scoped TrustPlane Passport — not a forever token.
3. For each call it attaches transcript-v1 proof binding the exact request: method, path, body hash, audience, route, and a nonce/time bucket.
4. A local verifier checks all of it and only then lets the request through. A stolen passport is nearly worthless: it expires in seconds, is scoped to one audience and request, and its jti is consumed once so it cannot be replayed.

## Ways to adopt it
- Brownfield adapter — a reverse-proxy verifier in front of an unmodified upstream API; the upstream code does not change.
- Library middleware — verify inside your own Go HTTP service.
- Broker + sidecar — a local broker issues request-bound passports; on Kubernetes it can require SPIFFE/SPIRE attested workload identity.

## Project status and where to get it
- TrustPlane Auth is in public preview. Caller-side SDKs are available for Go and Node.js (TypeScript); a Python SDK is planned.
- Source, SDKs, and examples: https://github.com/trustplane-dev
- Documentation: https://docs.auth.trustplane.dev
- Pricing: https://trustplane.dev/pricing.md — open-source runtime is $0 (MIT license, self-hosted, no mandatory phone-home). Managed fleet governance is a future/enterprise direction, not yet available.
- Note: managed fleet governance (signing, distribution, revocation, audit at scale) is a separate, future/enterprise direction and is not part of this open-source runtime.

## Pages
- [Home](https://trustplane.dev/): what proof-bound authorization is, the problem with machine secrets, how it works, use cases, and FAQ.
- [TrustPlane Auth](https://trustplane.dev/auth.html): the open-source runtime — passports, transcript-v1 request binding, replay protection, signed bundles, adapter/broker deployment, and audit events.
- [TrustPlane Control](https://trustplane.dev/control.html): the governance plane — enrollment, signed policy distribution, instant revocation, audit, multitenant fleets, RBAC, managed or self-hosted.
- [Solutions](https://trustplane.dev/solutions.html): AI agents, MCP and tool servers, service-to-service APIs, and partner machine clients.
- [Subscriptions](https://trustplane.dev/pricing.html): Auth (free preview), Control (managed subscription), Enterprise (self-hosted Control, SSO, SLAs).
- [Downloads](https://trustplane.dev/downloads.html): docs, GitHub, SDKs, and how to evaluate Auth in front of one API.
- [Documentation](https://docs.auth.trustplane.dev): setup and integration guidance.

## SDKs
- [Go SDK](https://github.com/trustplane-dev/trustplane-auth-sdk-go): sign proof-bound requests from Go services and agents.
- [TypeScript SDK](https://github.com/trustplane-dev/trustplane-auth-sdk-js): sign proof-bound requests from Node.js and TypeScript runtimes.
- Python SDK: planned, not yet released.

- How do you authorize AI agents that call APIs and tools?
- How is proof-bound authorization different from API keys and OAuth bearer tokens?
- Is TrustPlane Auth an identity provider?
- Where does enforcement happen?
- What is a secure alternative to API keys for machine-to-machine access?
- How do you authorize MCP / tool-server calls?
- How do you stop stolen or replayed machine credentials?
- How do you add request-level authorization in front of an existing API without rewriting it?
- What is proof-bound (request-bound) authorization?
- How do you authorize non-human identities such as agents, services, and workloads?
- Does TrustPlane Auth replace OAuth, IAM, or a service mesh?
- Do I need Kubernetes or a hosted service to run it?
- Does it work with SPIFFE, OIDC, and MCP?
- What is MCP authorization?
